articles.title: Gol suspende dois voos internacionais e um nacional em Fortaleza | G1
articles.standfirst: A empresa disse que as suspensões foram motivadas pelos 'aumentos sucessivos' no preço do combustível de aviação.
articles.summary: A empresa disse que as suspensões foram motivadas pelos 'aumentos sucessivos' no preço do combustível de aviação.
articles.body:
Gol suspende dois voos internacionais e um nacional em Fortaleza — Foto: Celso Tavares/G1

Apenas 15 meses após o anúncio de abertura, a companhia aérea Gol anunciou agora a suspensão dos voos diretos entre Fortaleza e Foz do Iguaçu , no Paraná; e entre a capital cearense e Montevidéu , capital do Uruguai . Também serão cancelados os voos entre Fortaleza e Orlando (EUA). As informações foram confirmadas pela Gol ao g1 nesta terça-feira (13).

Por meio de nota, a empresa afirmou que as rotas serão suspensas a partir de fevereiro de 2027 . A Gol disse que as suspensões foram motivadas pelos "aumentos sucessivos" no preço do combustível de aviação, conhecido como QAV, que hoje já representa cerca de 40% dos custos operacionais da companhia.

O QAV foi um dos combustíveis que mais encareceu com a guerra entre Estados Unidos e Irã. Dados divulgados pela Associação Brasileira das Empresas Aéreas (Abear) indicaram que os preços dos combustíveis de aviação já haviam crescido 49% até agosto por causa do conflito , que teve início no fim de fevereiro.

"Em razão dos aumentos sucessivos do preço do combustível de aviação (QAV), que dobrou e representa cerca de 40% dos custos operacionais da Companhia, a GOL está ajustando rotas, com redução e/ou suspensão da operação em alguns trechos. O planejamento de malha é um processo dinâmico e contínuo no setor de aviação comercial e ocorre rigorosamente de acordo com as necessidades da operação como um todo, sem qualquer distinção ou priorização regional por parte da companhia", disse a empresa.

A Gol disse ainda que vai oferecer outras opções de conexões para os clientes "por meio de voos com conexão ou em parceria com companhias aéreas parceiras, apoiada por sua ampla rede de mais de 60 acordos de codeshare e interline".

Aeroporto de Fortaleza — Foto: Agência Diário

O secretário de Turismo do Ceará, Gustavo Montenegro, lamentou a suspensão das rotos, que foram anunciadas em julho de 2025, mas destacou que "a reavaliação de rotas é constante no mundo da aviação". Ele também disse que o conflito no Oriente Médio pesou na decisão da empresa.

"Hoje, o turismo tem que estar se preocupando com geopolítica. Então, o conflito que tem lá no Oriente Médio está impactando aqui e o restante do turismo no mundo todo. Mas também abre um leque de oportunidades. Alguns voos que a Iberia, que é uma grande parceira nossa e que iniciou os voos em 2026, retirou voos lá do Oriente Médio e está ampliando as frequências aqui para o Ceará", destacou.

Montenegro disse que a Gol comunicou ao governo a suspensão das rotas devido ao aumento dos custos operacionais e destacou que, além de Fortaleza, várias outras rotas da Gol em aeroportos do Brasil também serão suspensas nos próximos meses. No caso do Ceará, ele disse, foram suspensas rotas que a companhia avaliou como pouco lucrativas.

"Todas essas três rotas, especificamente do Ceará, elas tinham um bom load factor, uma boa ocupação, Montevideo, Foz do Iguaçu e Orlando. Mas, ao ver a análise deles [da Gol], constam que é uma rota que não dá um tanto lucro como demais outras rotas para a empresa", explicou o secretário.

articles.title: Netflix acquires Spanish rights to 2030 men’s World Cup
articles.summary: Netflix’s long-rumored pursuit of the men’s World Cup produced a deal on Tuesday, though the streamer’s first foothold in FIFA’s biggest event comes in Spain...
articles.body:
Netflix's long-rumored pursuit of the men's World Cup produced a deal on Tuesday, though the streamer's first foothold in FIFA's biggest event comes in Spain rather than the United States.

According to The Athletic's Dan Sheldon and Philip Buckingham , Netflix has secured the Spanish rights to the 2030 World Cup and will stream all 104 matches of a 48-team tournament that Spain will host alongside Morocco and Portugal, with centenary matches in Uruguay, Paraguay, and Argentina.

Netflix won't wall off the entire tournament, however, as it will stream one match per matchday free of charge in Spain, and a national free-to-air broadcaster will receive a package headlined by every Spain match, along with both semifinals and the final.

As the Sports Business Journal's Austin Karp suggests, the Spanish arrangement could become Netflix's blueprint as it chases men's World Cup rights in other markets.

Until now, Netflix's World Cup rights were limited to the women's game.

In December 2024, the streamer won U.S. rights to the 2027 and 2031 Women's World Cups after Puck's John Ourand reported that an outsider placed the winning bid, taking over a tournament that Fox had aired in the U.S. since 2015. Netflix also holds Canadian rights to both tournaments.

In June, Netflix and FIFA released a World Cup video game on the platform to coincide with the start of this summer's men's tournament. And ahead of the 2027 Women's World Cup in Brazil next summer, Netflix has added Andrés Cantor , named Rebecca Lowe as host , held talks with Megan Rapinoe and Marta about analyst roles, and announced plans to broadcast the Women's World Cup draw live from Brazil in December .

Last month, Netflix Chief Content Officer Bela Bajaria told CNBC the company was open to discussing men's World Cup rights with FIFA.

"We have a great partnership and relationship with FIFA, so we're definitely always going to have those conversations," she said.

The biggest of those conversations still lies ahead, as FIFA has yet to sell U.S. rights to the 2030 and 2034 World Cups, and incumbents Fox and NBC, along with Disney, YouTube, Prime Video and Apple, have all reportedly shown interest. FIFA reportedly wants to package the English- and Spanish-language rights together , which would work in a streamer's favor, since Netflix can run both language feeds on a single platform while a traditional broadcaster would need separate channels. When our Drew Lerner handicapped the 2030 field in July, he rated Netflix the most likely streaming winner but questioned whether it would share inventory with a linear network.

In Spain, at least, Netflix has already answered that question by sharing the tournament's biggest matches with free television while keeping every game on its own platform.

articles.title: EFL Trophy: Richarlison scores for Spurs under-21s at Cheltenham
articles.summary: Out-of-favour Tottenham striker Richarlison scores for the club's under-21s in their EFL Trophy penalty defeat at Cheltenham.
articles.body:
Out-of-favour Tottenham striker Richarlison scored for the club's under-21s in their EFL Trophy defeat at Cheltenham Town.

The 29-year-old Brazil international had moves to Everton and Vasco da Gama collapse through this summer and has not been included in Spurs' 25-man Premier League squad.

His sole senior appearance for the club this season came in the 3-0 defeat at Brentford on the Premier League 's opening weekend in August.

After George Miller had given the League Two side the lead, Richarlison equalised with a tidy first-time finish from a right-wing cross.

Miracle Adewole then put the young Spurs side ahead in the group-stage tie, only for Miller to score deep into stoppage time to send the tie to penalties.

Richarlison scored his spot-kick but the home side won the shootout 7-6.

Goal crisis & in drop zone - so why is Spurs' £60m striker stuck in U21s?

Chelsea winners on tough night for young sides

Elsewhere, Notts County thumped the under-21s of city rivals Nottingham Forest 5-1 to secure their place in the second round.

Goals from Luka Smyth, Jacob Bedeau, Lee Ndlovu, Connor Grant and Callum Roberts put the League One side 5-0 up before Buba Sanneh got a consolation for the visitors in time added on.

Oldham are also through after they came back from behind to beat Leeds' under-21s 4-2 at Boundary Park.

Noah Chilvers scored from the spot put the League Two team in front before Callum Mills, 18, scored his fourth goal in two games in the competition to make it 1-1 at the break.

Carrick Njinko put the young Whites in front but goals from Kane Drummond, Josh Hawkes and Kai Payne saw the home side take the win.

Gillingham raced into a 4-0 lead against Brighton's under-21s before holding out for a 4-3 victory.

The Gills looked to be cruising to a thumping win thanks to goals from Tom Eaves, Bradley Dack, Ethan Coleman and Louie Dayal.

However, Shane Nti grabbed a double for the visitors and Tyler Silsby added a third in the final minute.

Fulham's under-21s also fell a goal short from a great comeback against League Two opposition as they lost 3-2 at Walsall.

A Tai Sodje double and a James Furlong goal had the Saddlers 3-0 up at half-time but Jonah Kusi-Asare and Dan Casey got the away side back in it after the interval.

Chelsea's under-21s did manage a win as they beat League One Reading 2-0 with a first-half double from Chizaram Ezenwata.

The Blues have five points from three games and will progress unless the Royals beat Bristol Rovers by four goals in the remaining game in that group.

articles.title: Alabama fans need to accept the truth about Kalen DeBoer after Georgia loss
articles.summary: In an odd way, Saturday's loss was so well-played by Alabama but with so much more room to grow that DeBoer might have finally turned a corner. He is Alabama...
articles.body:
Late in Saturday night's loss to Georgia, after cornerback Dijon Lee committed a boneheaded personal foul penalty that ended Alabama's chances of a comeback, we saw a side of coach Kalen DeBoer that doesn't often come out in public view.

As Lee returned to the sidelines and tried to avoid a confrontation with his coach, the normally stoic and understated DeBoer let loose, repeatedly yelling words that were easy to lip read — "You just cost us the game!" — until Lee finally stopped and paid attention.

For DeBoer's first two years following Nick Saban, every loss has felt like a referendum on whether he's the long-term answer or whether the most insatiable fan base in college football will chase him to another job where the pressure isn't as all-consuming.

But a funny thing happened after Alabama's 20-17 loss. Despite an intense game going sideways late, the discourse wasn't about whether DeBoer has what it takes to succeed at Alabama. As the video clip of his interaction with Lee circulated on social media, the debate instead revolved around whether DeBoer had gone too far by dressing down a player so aggressively in public.

In a strange way, that's progress. Because for the first time in a tough moment, it did not look like there was a placeholder wearing a black hoodie on the Alabama sideline. After a couple years of speculation about whether DeBoer would be fired or run to place like Michigan because he's not Saban, it felt definitively and conclusively like DeBoer's program.

This isn't a scientific conclusion, and it's admittedly strange to make it on the heels of a loss. But at some point, the evidence has to matter. And it points to the following:

Alabama's leadership believes strongly that DeBoer is the right coach.

DeBoer wants to be at Alabama for the long haul.

There is nobody in college football that Alabama could realistically hire who could do the job better.

It's time for all Alabama fans and, frankly, the college football gossip machine to finally accept it: DeBoer and Alabama are a good match, and he's not going anywhere anytime soon. Might as well sit back and try to enjoy the ride.

"I don't think many coaches in the country would want to go behind the great legendary coach he came in behind," Georgia coach Kirby Smart said last week. "That's a tough job, tough expectations, and he's done an incredible job in his own way and in his own rights."

No matter who athletic director Greg Byrne picked to follow Saban in January of 2024, it was going to take awhile for that person to settle into being The Alabama Coach regardless of immediate success.

Saban was just too big of a figure for 17 years for that transition to happen quickly. And he certainly hasn't made it any easier on his successor by still being everywhere all the time: On TV commercials, on Capitol Hill lobbying for the Protect College Sports Act, on ESPN's "College GameDay" and all the various shows attached to it.

If you're a college sports fan, you can't get away from him. And if you're DeBoer, you have to deal with all that — plus the fact Saban still has an office on campus, remains a presence in Tuscaloosa and is still the de facto symbol of Alabama football. This is not a quiet retirement away from the spotlight, it has been a roadblock to the psychological transition of closing the book on that era of dominance and resetting expectations for what Alabama football should be going forward.

Everyone knew that was going to be a challenge, and it's why there's been so much noise around DeBoer during two seasons that had good moments, but were ordinary in the end.

A year ago, as Alabama was preparing to play Oklahoma in the first round of the College Football Playoff, there was strong speculation in early December that Michigan was prepared to make a big run at DeBoer — a conversation that never really materialized because Alabama won that game and extended its season until New Year's Day. Even if there was mutual interest, Michigan had to move on.

Even now, one of the juicy bits of gossip you'll hear around the coaching carousel is that DeBoer would be the top choice at USC if it pulls the plug on Lincoln Riley. The logic behind this rumor is rooted in DeBoer's prior relationship with USC athletic director Jen Cohen, who hired him at Washington after the 2021 season.

But that theory doesn't really hold up to scrutiny. In April of this year, Alabama extended DeBoer's contract through the 2032 season at an average annual salary of $12.5 million per season. If he were to leave, it would cost DeBoer $10 million to get out of the contract until Jan. 31, 2027, and $8 million the following year.

That's a lot of money to give up for a job that isn't going to pay him more and isn't going to give him any better chance at winning a national title, especially in the era of playoff expansion where a well-run Alabama program is going to be in the tournament every year unless disaster strikes.

There's also going to be a timing issue if the USC job opens up. Alabama, currently ranked No. 6, looks like a good bet to go 10-2 at worst. The Tide should once again be playing on Jan. 1 or likely beyond, which would again make the USC job moot if it opens up. With the transfer portal being open from Jan. 4-13, athletic directors can't really afford to wait.

And this is all by design. Alabama administrators did not give DeBoer a contract extension because he was overwhelmingly successful in his first two seasons. He hasn't even come close yet to winning a national title. They did it because, for the people who matter, Saban's successor has been settled. The contract is simply a fire extinguisher.

Byrne is a proponent of stability and a strong believer that buyouts work. Anyone suggesting that Alabama isn't attached to DeBoer or that he wants to get out of town needs the face the financial reality of the situation. He's not going anywhere, nor should he.

Alabama fans, who ran off several coaches between Bear Bryant and Saban, might be coming around to that new reality. This is a different era. Even Saban couldn't recreate today what he built in the 2010s.

At some point in the future, maybe DeBoer proves that he's not going to lead Alabama where it ultimately wants to go. But the data so far suggests that he's going to have a team that's in the mix every year, and with a quarterback he's developed from the beginning in Keelon Russell, Alabama is starting to look like the souped-up, five-star version of what he had at Washington.

Slowly but surely, the product on the field is taking on the personality of the coach. And at the end of that Georgia game, DeBoer showed a side of that personality he often suppresses when the cameras are on. While there were certainly some critics suggesting that he went too far and demeaned Lee, it's hard to make that case when we saw Saban light up players and assistant coaches many times, using words that you would not bring to the Sunday dinner table.

It's called coaching. Even in an era where players make a lot of money, it's still necessary.

"We preach emotional maturity and I really feel strong that across the board we had that with our team and would have never expected that to happen," DeBoer said. "You've got to give yourself a chance. We've been pretty good at that the last two years and obviously the moment comes up like we had just now, we didn't respond."

Coaching evaluations this time of year are often a little bit like fantasy football. It's fun to project how somebody with a well-known track record might fit at another program or why they may have an interest in leaving their current job for another one.

Every now and then we do get a massive coaching move like Lane Kiffin going from Ole Miss to LSU last season. But for the most part, the reality is boring.

And Alabama's reality is that DeBoer is now their guy and everyone better get on board.

In an odd way, Saturday's loss to Georgia was so well played by Alabama but with so much more room to grow that DeBoer might have turned that conversation in his favor more than with any of the wins he's had there.

It finally looked and felt like DeBoer's program in every way we can measure. Anyone hanging on to the fantasy of something different or appreciably better is chasing a ghost and wasting their time.

articles.body:
Última hora del Estados Unidos - España en directo

MUUUUUUYYYY BUENAAAAS NOCHEEEEESS . Jornada nocturna la que nos toca hoy para volver a ver a la selección española femenina, que se mide de nuevo frente a Estados Unidos en un amistoso para medir fuerzas de cara al Mundial del año que viene. El encuentro disputado entre ambas el pasado 10 de octubre acabó con 0-2 a favor de las nuestras, goles de Patri Guijarro y Eva Navarro.

El partido del sábado fue la segunda ocasión en el que las nacionales han conseguido ganar a las norteamericanas en los cinco partidos disputados. La primera fue en 2022, en un amistoso de preparación para el Mundial que terminaron trayendo a España. Esperemos que se repita la situación. Si hoy consiguen la victoria, se empatará el historial.

¿Quién conseguirá llevarse la victoria? Te lo contamos aquí, en MARCA .

articles.title: Hansi Flick: "Lamine no ha marcado, pero ha estado excelente"
articles.standfirst: El alemán destaca el gran partido del delantero azulgrana
articles.summary: El alemán destaca el gran partido del delantero azulgrana
articles.body: Hansi Flick estaba muy contento después del contundente triunfo que consiguió su equipo en un campo siempre complicado como es el Ali Sami Yen. El técnico destacó el trabajo que hizo Lamine Yamal que estuvo a un nivel excelente en la segunda mitad siendo clave en los goles que consiguió el equipo azulgrana. "Estamos muy contentos con el resultado. La primera parte también hemos jugado bien. Tuvieron una oportunidad y marcaron. Hemos conseguido volver y eso ha sido muy importante". "Creo que en la Champions cuando jugamos bien, en algunas situaciones, no tomamos buenas decisiones en el último tercio. Eso hay que mejorarlo. En este estadio, con este ambiente, no era fácil pero estoy muy contento". "Lamine no ha marcado hoy pero sí que ha dado ese último pase en dos goles y ha estado excelente. Es un jugador increíble y muy importante para nosotros". "Físicamente está preparado. Es un jugador importante y es bueno tenerlo en el césped". "Se queda en el vestuario"

articles.title: El preparador físico de Mourinho: "No es bipolar... es exigente"
articles.standfirst: Carlos Lalín compartió con José Mourinho las etapas del Real Madrid, el Chelsea, el Manchester United, el Tottenham
articles.summary: Carlos Lalín compartió con José Mourinho las etapas del Real Madrid, el Chelsea, el Manchester United, el Tottenham
articles.body: Carlos Lalín conoce a José Mourinho más allá de los focos, las ruedas de prensa y los titulares que acompañan al entrenador portugués. Durante años formó parte de su equipo de trabajo en el Real Madrid y después en Inglaterra. Una larga etapa junto a uno de los técnicos más exigentes del fútbol mundial que le permite ofrecer una perspectiva privilegiada sobre su liderazgo, su gestión del vestuario y su manera de entender el rendimiento. Nacido en Caracas y vinculado profesionalmente al fútbol desde A Coruña, Lalín ha desarrollado su carrera entre la preparación física, la readaptación y el trabajo multidisciplinar en la élite. En la noche previa al Roma-Real Madrid, el preparador pasó por Otra Ronda, el programa de Radio MARCA presentado por Carlos Vicente, 'Chitu', para repasar su experiencia junto a Mourinho, analizar las lesiones en el fútbol de máximo nivel y explicar por qué la profesionalidad de Cristiano Ronaldo constituye un ejemplo para las nuevas generaciones. «Lo conozco en el Real Madrid, cuando me ficha el club. Desde el principio se establece una buena conexión con el equipo de trabajo y estoy a sus órdenes durante tres años. Cuando finaliza mi contrato en el Madrid, me llama para unirme a ellos en Inglaterra y empezar una aventura y una experiencia fabulosa, hasta que llegamos a Roma. Allí decidimos seguir caminos diferentes». "Si tienes un jefe que exige y exprime a todo el equipo de trabajo, evidentemente eso tiene consecuencias. Pero ese modelo también puede atraer un rendimiento a corto plazo. Hay un libro muy interesante, de un autor español, que habla de aprender de los campeones a partir de cuatro conceptos: querer, poder, saber y demostrar. Quien busca la excelencia quiere, puede, sabe y lo demuestra". En vísperas de su enfrentamiento con el Real Madrid, vuelve a hablarse del carácter de Mourinho. Un día parece enfadado con todo y al siguiente transmite una confianza absoluta. ¿Es tan imprevisible como parece desde fuera? "Yo volvería a lo que comentábamos antes: el escenario y el teatro. Mañana vamos a estar en un escenario tremendamente emocional. Conozco Roma, Trigoria, el club y la unión que existe entre el equipo y su afición. Estamos ante dos entrenadores con metodologías y aproximaciones diferentes, pero cada uno utiliza sus armas". "Mourinho, ante todo, es una persona y un líder que cuida de sus soldados. Utilizará las estrategias que considere necesarias para vencer, que es lo que se busca para construir y crecer. No definiría a una persona como bipolar. Es consciente del reto que tiene por delante, que no es fácil". "Es un escenario tremendamente emocional. Conozco Roma, Trigoria y la relación del club con su afición. Es un contexto que puede tener mucha influencia. También estamos ante dos entrenadores con metodologías diferentes y una forma distinta de aproximarse al juego. Cada uno utilizará sus herramientas para intentar ganar». Lalín ha trabajado en algunos de los clubes más importantes de Europa y ha conocido a futbolistas de primer nivel. ¿Hubo alguno que le llamara especialmente la atención por su preocupación por el estado físico? "Cristiano Ronaldo. Siempre se cuidaba, se preocupaba y se ocupaba. No lo destaco solamente por lo que representa futbolísticamente, sino porque es un perfil de jugador que ha sabido prolongar su vida deportiva gracias a su enorme profesionalidad". "No necesariamente. Si revisamos la literatura científica y conocemos otras realidades, vemos que las lesiones en el deporte de élite son, en ocasiones, inevitables. Hay que asumir que existe un riesgo. En partidos y equipos de máxima exigencia, no solo física, sino también emocional, ese riesgo puede tener una mayor incidencia".

articles.title: Baptista defiende a Vinicius: "Es una pena que duden de él..."
articles.standfirst: El ex jugador de Real Madrid y Roma pasó por los micrófonos de 'Otra Ronda' en Radio MARCA
articles.summary: El ex jugador de Real Madrid y Roma pasó por los micrófonos de 'Otra Ronda' en Radio MARCA
articles.body: Julio Baptista tiene claro que el Real Madrid necesita a Vinicius. El exfutbolista brasileño, que defendió las camisetas del conjunto blanco y de la Roma, salió en defensa de su compatriota en la víspera del enfrentamiento entre ambos equipos en la Champions League. En una entrevista en Otra Ronda, el programa de Radio MARCA presentado por Carlos Vicente, 'Chitu', reclamó comprensión hacia un jugador que, a su juicio, ha demostrado sobradamente su compromiso con el madridismo y merece el respaldo de la afición cuando atraviesa un momento complicado. «Creo que Vinicius ha dado bastante al Madrid. Ha hecho méritos propios para tener el cariño del aficionado y, si en un momento no está bien, tanto sus compañeros como la afición deben arroparle para que vuelva a estar en ese estado óptimo y perfecto para ayudar al Madrid a conseguir lo que más quiere el madridismo, que es seguir ganando títulos», explicó Baptista. El brasileño fue todavía más contundente al valorar la importancia del extremo para el futuro del equipo blanco: «Es más fácil seguir ganando títulos con Vinicius que sin él». Una declaración de intenciones en un momento en el que el rendimiento y la situación del futbolista están bajo el foco de la actualidad madridista. Baptista quiso poner el acento en la dimensión humana del fútbol y en la presión que soportan los jugadores de un club como el Real Madrid. El exdelantero considera que, en ocasiones, se olvida que detrás de los futbolistas hay personas que también sufren y atraviesan dificultades. «El Madrid es un club donde se exige mucho al jugador y todo el mundo quiere que lo dé todo en todo momento. Pero a veces las personas no entienden que los jugadores sienten, lloran y tienen dolor. Parece que creen que son extraterrestres», reflexionó. El brasileño, que conoce de primera mano las exigencias de vestir la camiseta blanca, insistió en que el apoyo puede ser determinante para recuperar la mejor versión de un futbolista. Su mensaje para Vinicius es claro: confianza, respaldo y paciencia para que vuelva a ofrecer todo su talento al equipo. La defensa del extremo llegó también después de que José Mourinho, al que Baptista conoce por su trayectoria en el fútbol europeo, se refiriera a la situación del brasileño. El exjugador prefirió centrarse en lo que considera fundamental para el Real Madrid: recuperar al futbolista y aprovechar todo lo que puede aportar. La entrevista se produjo en la noche previa al duelo entre la Roma y el Real Madrid, dos clubes que forman parte de la trayectoria de Baptista. El brasileño guarda un cariño especial por ambos, aunque reconoce que el conjunto blanco ocupa un lugar destacado en su vida. «Tengo un cariño muy grande por los clubes en los que he jugado. Es verdad que el Madrid ocupa un lugar muy especial en mi vida», reconoció. Sin embargo, su nueva perspectiva como entrenador le lleva a analizar los partidos desde otro punto de vista: «Hoy veo el fútbol mucho más desde la interpretación de un entrenador. Me fijo en lo que han intentado promover los técnicos, en las dinámicas que proyectan para el partido y en aspectos más profundos del juego». Sobre el encuentro del Olímpico, Baptista advirtió de la dificultad que encontrará el equipo madridista ante una afición que empuja durante los 90 minutos. «La afición de la Roma es muy fuerte y está empujando todo el partido. Jugar ahí no es fácil para el Madrid», señaló. Aun así, espera que el conjunto blanco responda a las expectativas que siempre acompañan al equipo en la máxima competición europea. «El Madrid es el equipo que todo el mundo quiere batir y esperamos que dé el nivel que se le exige en la Champions y haga frente a la Roma». Baptista también reflexionó sobre la presión que rodea a los técnicos de los grandes clubes y, en particular, sobre la figura de Mourinho. El brasileño considera que dirigir al Real Madrid exige unas habilidades que van mucho más allá de los conocimientos tácticos. «Ser entrenador del Madrid requiere una habilidad especial, sobre todo para lidiar con la prensa y con todo el entorno. No es fácil», apuntó. El exfutbolista, que está dando sus primeros pasos como técnico, tuvo además la oportunidad de recibir clases de Luis de la Fuente durante su formación como entrenador. Del actual seleccionador español se quedó con una enseñanza que considera esencial para cualquier profesional del banquillo: tener las ideas claras. «Lo más importante que me pudo dejar es que el entrenador tiene que tener las cosas muy claras. Creo que eso es lo más importante que pude aprender de él», explicó Baptista, que valoró la experiencia de haber tenido como profesor al técnico que ha llevado a España a conquistar grandes éxitos internacionales. Actualmente, Baptista trabaja en el São Paulo, el club en el que se formó, ayudando a los jóvenes futbolistas en su desarrollo. Un regreso a casa que afronta con ilusión y con la intención de crecer como entrenador antes de dar nuevos pasos en su carrera. «He vuelto a casa y ahora mismo estoy trabajando aquí, en el club del que salí. Estoy muy contento y muy feliz de poder ayudar a los chicos», explicó. Su futuro no está limitado a Brasil. Baptista tiene claro que quiere consolidarse en los banquillos y no descarta regresar algún día al fútbol español, una competición que marcó su trayectoria como jugador. «Sé que llegaré a ser entrenador. Lo que quiero es hacerlo bien. He vuelto a mi país para tener la oportunidad de crecer y, cuando llegue una oportunidad fuera de Brasil, también quiero hacerlo bien, sea en España, en Inglaterra o donde sea», afirmó. Y dejó abierta una puerta que le haría especial ilusión: «Tengo un cariño muy grande por la Liga española porque fue la competición que me proyectó al fútbol mundial. Si algún día se da la situación de volver a España como entrenador, sería muy bonito hacerlo de la misma manera que lo hice como jugador». Mientras construye esa nueva etapa en los banquillos, Baptista no olvida su pasado en el Real Madrid ni su vínculo con la Roma. Dos camisetas que volverán a cruzarse en Europa y ante las que el brasileño tiene una petición muy clara para el madridismo: confiar en Vinicius. Porque, como resume el exdelantero, el camino hacia los títulos resulta más sencillo con el talento del brasileño sobre el campo que sin él.

articles.title: Millwall 0-1 Swansea: Ronald winner keeps Vitor Matos' side top - but game disrupted by alleged racist chanting
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Millwall and Swansea at The Den on Tuesday; Ronald's winner keeps Vitor Matos' side top, but game disrupted by alleged racist chanting
articles.body:
Referee Edward Duckworth halted the match in the 65th minute and walked to the dug-outs at the Den to speak with Lions boss Alex Neil, Swans counterpart Vitor Matos and fourth official Ruebyn Ricardo. Eom had been warming up as a substitute at the time.

A security guard was also on the scene, with referee Duckworth seeming to point to an area in the stands behind the Swansea dug-out.

When play eventually resumed after almost seven minutes it was announced in the stadium that there had been a report of racist chanting, adding that police were working to identify any offenders using CCTV.

The game itself had a dramatic finale with table-topping Swansea scoring a last-gasp winner.

Swansea arrived in south London with the best defensive record in the division and they showed why as Millwall dominated the first half.

The Lions should have gone ahead after 10 minutes when Mark Sykes crossed low to Kyrell Lisbie, who looked set for a tap-in until Filip Lissah made a last-ditch tackle.

Moments later Jenson Metcalfe thought he was through on goal but this time on-loan Sunderland defender Jenson Seelt, making his first Swans start, got back to make a vital challenge.

A neat flick from Lyndon Dykes then teed up Sykes six yards out but Swans goalkeeper Lawrence Vigouroux made a fine save.

Vigouroux then came for and missed a Metcalfe corner, but Jordi Osei-Tutu's header was deflected onto the roof of the net.

Swansea managed just one shot on target in a one-sided first half, a tame effort from Zan Vipotnik which was easily dealt with by Lions keeper Filip Marschall.

The visitors got a sniff of a chance early in the second half after Derek Mazou-Sacko was booked for a foul on Moussa Yeo, but Josh Tymon sent the free-kick over the crossbar.

Lions captain Jake Cooper then had to hack Joseph Opoku's shot off the line before Yeo fired narrowly over as the leaders began to exert more authority.

Vipotnik slipped in Yeo but Cooper was on hand to make a timely interception, before Mazou-Sacko made another goal-line clearance to deny Ross Stewart.

After the delay in play, Millwall searched for a winner and Vigouroux made a point-blank save to deny Dykes and Tristan Crama headed the resulting corner over.

But Swansea nicked it at the death when Opoku crossed, Millwall hesitated and Brazilian winger Ronald crashed home the winner.

"I'm disappointed. I didn't think we deserved to lose.

"First half I thought we were the team looking threatening and they were under the cosh. But we didn't take our chances."

"I think it was a lucky substitution by the manager.

"It was a really intense game, a good game, Millwall started really well. But I think we did it really well to deal with that, we stayed organised. That allowed us to grow into the game."

articles.title: Women's World Cup play-off final: Pressure on Norway, says Wales boss Rhian Wilkinson
articles.summary: Rhian Wilkinson says the pressure will be on Gemma Grainger's Norway in their Women's World Cup play-off final against Wales in December.
articles.body:
Rhian Wilkinson says the pressure will be on Gemma Grainger's Norway in their Women's World Cup play-off final against Wales in December.

Wales moved a step closer to reaching the Women's World Cup for the first time as a 3-0 win over Albania in Llanelli secured a 4-0 aggregate success in their play-off semi-final.

Wales now face a step up in a class as they take on a Norway side ranked 14th in the world, but Wilkinson insists Wales can "absolutely" cause an upset as they are reunited with former boss Grainger.

"The pressure is always on the big nations and that's something I think we thrive on," said the Wales head coach.

"We're a small nation, we fight for each other. You see some of the play tonight [against Albania] any you'd be proud of [that] from any team in world.

"[There were some] fantastic levels of play and that's with probably one of the younger teams that's playing in this competition right now, so I think it's an exciting time and why not be excited about the possibility."

The play-off final first leg will be played at the Cardiff City Stadium on Tuesday, 1 December before the return leg in Norway four days later.

Norway, the 1995 world champions, have reached every Women's World Cup since the tournament began in 1991.

They will begin as firm favourites against Wales, who are ranked 17 places below them by Fifa and who have never beaten a top-20 ranked side in a competitive fixture.

But Wilkinson insists Wales, whose only previous major championship appearance was at Euro 2025, can cause Norway problems.

"They're a team that's performing well, that's doing well, as are we and we've got some fantastic players that can absolutely go toe-to-toe with them," she added.

"I've just talked to the staff I think everyone needs a few days off to rest and recover.

"Then we're going to go again, do the best we can to deliver a team that's going to fight for their country."

The complex nature of the qualifying process means that even if they were to upset Norway, Wales may not be guaranteed a place at next year's World Cup.

Depending on which other sides come through the eight European play-off finals, Wales may have to negotiate an inter-confederation play-off next February to secure their spot in Brazil.

"The World Cup is off in the distance - I'll keep saying that because we don't even know if and when we beat Norway if that's the final hurdle," Wilkinson said.

"So it is the next game in front of us - we don't get too far ahead. It's the next job and we've got a lot of work to do as a staff."

Mayzee Davies, Elise Hughes and Hannah Cain found the target as Wales eased to victory over Albania having limped over the line in the first leg last Friday.

"I think we know that the performance away wasn't one that we were particularly pleased with," Wilkinson said.

"I thought we lacked intensity, lacked teeth in our defending, we weren't connecting our passes in a way I know we can.

"Tonight was the absolute reversal of that. I thought from the first minute Angharad [James] led her team in an intense, strong performance where the team really showed what they're capable of. It was fun to watch."

articles.title: Lisandro Martinez attacks Man Utd board after Atletico Madrid defeat
articles.summary: Lisandro Martinez launches a blistering attack on Manchester United's hierarchy for not strengthening the squad following qualification for the Champions League.
articles.body:
Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez has launched a blistering attack on the club's hierarchy for not strengthening the squad following qualification for the Champions League.

Tuesday's 2-0 defeat by Atletico Madrid means United have now gone five games without a win.

Their most recent victory was against Azerbaijani champions Sabah FK on 10 September. United's only other win in nine matches this season came against newly promoted Ipswich at Old Trafford, when they had to come from behind.

The Red Devils finished third in the Premier League last term to seal a Champions League return for the first time in three years.

They won 12 of Michael Carrick's 17 games in interim charge following the dismissal of Ruben Amorim in January, which was enough to earn the former United midfielder a permanent two-year contract as head coach .

"We did a fantastic season last season and now we expect more from the top, more players to compete because many teams bring many players as well," Martinez told Amazon Prime.

"Atletico have an amazing team and they deserved to win today.

"I expect more [investment]. 100%. I expect more from our technical director [Jason Wilcox].

"I have to be honest, as players we have to do more but it is also important when you make a strong squad to be ready for this kind of night.

"Tonight it is easy to [blame] the coach, easy to say the players but also we have to see other areas."

Martinez's view has been echoed by many external observers and has also been mentioned by some inside Old Trafford.

The failure to bring in striking support for Benjamin Sesko and competition at left-back for Luke Shaw have both been highlighted in a summer when United spent £155m on three midfielders to the exclusion of any other position.

Minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe was sitting next to United chief executive Omar Berrada in the Metropolitano Stadium on Tuesday.

They have sacked managers in the past two seasons after backing them the previous summer, with Erik ten Hag dismissed in October 2024, before Amorim was shown the exit door in January 2026.

"You can't keep changing, changing, changing the manager," said Martinez. "What about other areas? I can't say more.

"Last season we did everything, we created the base to create an amazing team."

Martinez's comments echo similar ones made by his Argentina defensive partner Cristian Romero against the Tottenham board last season.

Ironically, Romero was in Atletico's side against United after his summer move to Spain.

Martinez, meanwhile, has one year left on his United contract and has yet to agree an extension.

Former United players Wayne Rooney and Ashley Young were in Madrid for the game.

Discussing Martinez's comments on Amazon Prime, both said the defender had gone too far and the damage inside the dressing room could be significant.

"Something like that will rip that dressing room apart," said Rooney.

The former England and United captain recalled his own public criticism of the club in 2010 which drew a fierce response from boss Sir Alex Ferguson.

Rooney said it had been a mistake which he had apologised for.

"It is disrespectful to his team-mates," he said. "He is saying his team-mates aren't good enough.

"Bruno [Fernandes] is the only one with any right to say that. Behind closed doors, it happens - but that interview isn't going to help...

"[Martinez] has tried to speak on behalf of the players but done it the wrong way.

"It looks like a player trying to look after himself. It was very premeditated. It is sad because you need everyone to stick together, you need to be as one."

Tielemans - who United bought from Aston Villa for £35m in July - also spoke to the host broadcaster but opted not to respond to the question.

Commentating on the game, and speaking before Martinez, former England striker Alan Shearer said he felt Carrick had been let down.

Young feels Martinez should have kept his counsel.

"We know recruitment has to work and be better but players have to be better," he said. "They are the ones who have to produce.

"There's going to be no change now. That could create [issues] all week after what was a good performance."

Speaking on BBC Radio 5 Live, former England keeper Paul Robinson said he could understand Martinez's point.

"I question his timing because with the noise around Manchester United at the moment, positivity needs to come out of the dressing room," he said.

"But on the flip side, I actually quite like it - a player being honest.

"Manchester United fans don't need their players coming out saying 'we're doing OK, the squad's strong enough'.

"Everyone can see they didn't recruit well enough and they need more players and the squad's not strong enough."

Although United were much improved on their tepid display against Tottenham at the weekend, conceding inside the first minute did not reflect well on Carrick.

And they have now gone five games without a win for the first time since 2024-25, when it happened under both Ten Hag and Amorim.

Carrick remains under intense pressure, although Martinez's words will bring renewed focus on Wilcox.

The former Southampton executive's appointment as football director is starting to be questioned, as are decisions taken by Ratcliffe and Berrada since the Glazer family stepped back despite remaining as majority shareholders.

In addition to sacking Ten Hag and Amorim, they also dismissed highly respected Dan Ashworth in December 2024 just five months after his appointment as sporting director.

Ratcliffe has also been blamed for increasing ticket prices and launching what the club said was a ticket touting investigation among season ticket holders, but which fans felt was an attempt to drive them out in favour of 'tourist' supporters.

In their latest set of accounts, United's overall debt stood at £1.1bn, with some fans criticising the decision to spend £63.5m on land for a new 100,000-capacity stadium - which is set to cost in excess of £2bn - rather than use the money to strengthen Carrick's squad.

United have only qualified for the Champions League in successive seasons twice sinceFerguson retired in 2013.

Amorim told Wilcox to concentrate on his own job in a blistering final news conference as United boss , when he suggested too much attention was paid to external "noise" from the likes of ex-player Gary Neville.

Carrick was initially asked for his response to Martinez's remarks live on TV, before heading to the post-match news conference where he was questioned about the comments by three different reporters.

"I haven't seen the interview," he said. "I've half heard about it. It's a bit about the emotions of the game.

"Straight after the game is not the time to talk about that interview and I can't really comment on that. It's important for us to move forward quickly.

"As group, I don't doubt the togetherness and us wanting to win. I know results-wise, it's easy to look and think there's something deeply wrong, but the players have been great in their willing."

Asked if he would speak to Martinez about his comments, Carrick said: "I need to find out a bit more about it before I can say if and what is going to be done."

'Brave' or 'shocking' - what you thought

Mark: Wow, very brave for Martinez for call out the upper management like that. I'm sure it won't go down well within Manchester United but I am also sure fans will be happy that someone in the club is finally saying it in public.

Stuart McLean: Martinez is right, refreshing to hear an honest assessment. Rooney and Young being unhappy and 'should be kept in the boardroom' are so wrong, we pay their astronomical wages. We should praise the honesty, as we all know the problems.

Ben Dutton: Martinez saying what most of the fans think. The rot starts at the top, and the squad is not up to the task. Rare honesty from a modern player!

Andrew Mitchell: Might be the best thing Lisandro has done in a United shirt. But the ownership are still there against the wishes of nearly every United fan, they continue to run the club the way they want (to its detriment), so there's no need to think Martinez's words will move them.

Joel Sparks: Martinez might be correct about the people at the top not doing enough. But their lack of activity is not causing his poor performances. Solanke didn't get the better of him on Saturday because of a lack of subs. He needs to give his head a wobble.

Dave Barry: It feels shocking to hear Martinez speak so openly. Those are criticisms fans have been chatting about in the pub for years - hearing it from a player's mouth is staggering.

articles.body: Pedri no pudo acabar el partido frente al Galatasaray. El canario pidió el cambio. Pero no fue ninguna lesión como el propio jugador explicó a la conclusión del encuentro en palabras en Movistar. El centrocampista hizo un gran partido y fue junto a Lamine el mejor del choque. "Teníamos la pelota y veíamos mucho espacio y nos jugábamos el último pase. Era darle unas vueltas y que entrase la gente de arriba. Cuando la tienen ellos cerca de arriba, son decisivos". "Tenemos mucha confianza. Se hablaba de que si no teníamos gol pero estamos demostrando que esta plantilla lo tiene. Solo es el comienzo de la temporada, a seguir". "Creo que siempre se especula pero está claro que podemos hacer muchos goles. Tenemos mucha gente de calidad que entra también desde el banquillo. La plantilla es muy amplia y muy buena. Se está viendo". "Vienen partidos muy importantes. Es el inicio de temporada pero son importantes. A disfrutarlos y sobre todo a ganar".

articles.title: El abogado de la hija de Maradona pide absolver al psicólogo e investigar a otras cuatro personas
articles.standfirst: "Maradona tenía una enfermedad grave pero tratable, no estaba condenado a morir", dijo Linfante,
articles.summary: "Maradona tenía una enfermedad grave pero tratable, no estaba condenado a morir", dijo Linfante,
articles.body: Félix Linfante, abogado de una de las hijas de Diego Armando Maradona, pidió este martes en sus alegatos del juicio por la muerte del astro la absolución del psicólogo Carlos Díaz y la apertura de una investigación contra otras cuatro personas que no están imputadas en la causa. "Maradona tenía una enfermedad grave pero tratable, no estaba condenado a morir", dijo Linfante, abogado de Jana Maradona, al comienzo de su alegato, en el que repasó de manera pormenorizada las responsabilidades de cada uno de los acusados. Para el médico de cabecera, Leopoldo Luque, la coordinadora de cuidados domiciliarios de la empresa de medicina Swiss Medical, Nancy Forlini, y la psiquiatra Agustina Cosachov pidió la mismas penas que la Fiscalía: doce, diez y ocho años de prisión, respectivamente, además de la inhabilitación profesional por diez años para los tres. A su vez, pidió penas de tres años de prisión y seis de inhabilitación para el jefe de enfermeros Mariano Perroni y el enfermero Ricardo Almirón. Al igual que el Ministerio Público Fiscal y el resto de las querellas, pidió la absolución del médico clínico Pedro Di Spagna, pero se diferenció de todos ellos al pedir también retirar los cargos contra el psicólogo Carlos Díaz. "Al tratarse de un psicólogo sin competencia para valorar el cuadro clínico, incorporado tardíamente al equipo y sin poder de decisión del tratamiento médico, desde esta parte vamos a proponer que se disponga su absolución", argumentó Linfante. El abogado dijo además que existieron "dos frentes autónomos" a cargo del tratamiento domiciliario que Maradona recibió en las dos semanas previas a su muerte, el 25 de noviembre de 2020, poco después de ser intervenido por un hematoma subdural en la cabeza. Según describió, los médicos personales junto a los asistentes de Maradona, por un lado, y la empresa de medicina Swiss Medical, por el otro, "se arrojaban la responsabilidad de un grupo a otro, usando como escudo a la familia". Por otra parte, Linfante solicitó al tribunal que se utilizara la evidencia surgida en el juicio para investigar a los asistentes del astro Maximiliano Pomargo y Vanesa Morla. "Maradona vivió sus últimos años rodeado de un entorno tóxico y nocivo, que lejos de cuidarlo y protegerlo se ocupaba de aislarlo", dijo el letrado, que se sumó así al pedido más temprano de Mario Baudry, abogado del menor de los hijos de Maradona y que también apuntó contra el equipo de asistentes del 'Diez'. Linfante afirmó que Pomargo, lejos de ser un mero asistente, "decidió con Luque cuándo, dónde y rodeado de quién estaría Diego" después de su última intervención y lo acusó también de haber ocultado el estado del paciente a sus familiares. Respecto a Vanesa Morla, destacó que "intervino en el dispositivo (de tratamiento) y se opuso a la internación que la familia pedía". El abogado también solicitó que fueran investigados Mariana Flichman, médica legista y gerente de riesgos de Swiss Medical, y Pablo Dimitroff, director de una clínica perteneciente a la misma empresa, ambos apuntados por su participación en la diagramación del tratamiento domiciliario. Los alegatos continuarán este miércoles con las querellas de las hijas del astro Dalma y Gianinna Maradona y de las hermanas del exfutbolita, Rita, Ana y Mabel Maradona.

articles.title: Arsenal beat Lille 3-0 as perfect Champions League start continues
articles.summary: Jurrien Timber, Eberechi Eze and Bukayo Saka score as Arsenal overcome Lille in UEFA Champions League.
articles.body:
Arsenal blew away Lille with a three-goal blitz in seven second-half minutes for a 3-0 win to extend their perfect start to the Champions League on Tuesday.

Jurrien Timber’s deft finish opened the floodgates just after the hour mark at the Emirates Stadium before Eberechi Eze and Bukayo Saka rounded off the scoring.

Victory takes Arsenal into a share of the lead at the top of the Champions League table alongside Barcelona and Sporting Lisbon.

Mikel Arteta was able to use the wealth of resources at his disposal as he made five changes to the side that beat Leeds 2-1 on Saturday.

But it was Lille boss Davide Ancelotti, son of Brazil coach Carlo Ancelotti, who was the happier after a goalless first half.

The visitors even had the ball in the net but Ayase Ueda was flagged offside.

Bruno Guimaraes came closest to breaking the deadlock for Arsenal before the break when he fired wide from close range and then saw a powerful shot from range parried by Berke Ozer.

The Gunners quickly went through the gears in the second period once Timber dinked the ball over Ozer from Noni Madueke’s pass.

Arteta had left arguably his three most potent attacking weapons on the bench and the introduction of Saka, Kai Havertz and Martin Odegaard made an immediate impact.

Saka’s low cross picked out Eze whose deflected shot flew into the top corner to end any doubt over the destiny of the three points.

The England winger then finished off an exquisite team move from Havertz’s cut-back for Arsenal’s third.

There were further cheers from the home fans when Olivier Giroud came on as a late substitute for Lille on his return to the club, where he scored 105 goals in a six-year spell.

But Giroud could not conjure up another Emirates goal as Lille remain without a Champions League point after their defeat to Real Betis on matchday one.

articles.title: Women's World Cup play-offs: 'Unplayable' Georgia Stanway proves a 'warrior' for England
articles.summary: Whatever the game, whatever the result, Georgia Stanway always seems to score for England.
articles.body:
Whatever the game, whatever the result, Georgia Stanway always seems to score for England.

Manager Sarina Wiegman called the midfielder a "warrior" after her performance against Greece helped seal an impressive 5-0 victory to complete an 8-1 aggregate triumph.

Stanway scored in both matches as the Lionesses progressed to round two of the Women's World Cup qualifying play-offs with ease.

She opened the scoring in Crete as they won 3-1 and when Wiegman called for more ruthlessness in Leicester, Stanway delivered again.

The 27-year-old is quickly becoming one of England's most important players. So what makes her so effective in front of goal?

Lionesses advance after comfortable win against Greece

Stanway's strikes in the last five days capped off a season in which she finished as England's top scorer and netted 11 times in her last 11 matches.

She also ranks inside the top three for most goals scored by European players in international football since Euro 2025.

While Wiegman was frustrated by her side's lack of ruthlessness in Greece, Stanway always looked dangerous and made sure she got on the scoresheet.

It felt inevitable she would join in the fun in Leicester when Alessia Russo and Lauren James grabbed a double each.

Stanway came close to matching them when the Arsenal midfielder coolly took control of a long ball inside the box with one deft touch and, with the second, fired it powerfully into the bottom corner.

It would have been the perfect strike to mark an impressive few days but it was ruled out for offside, much to Wiegman's dismay.

"She is always so eager to go towards goal. She has that tenacity in her," said the England boss when asked about Stanway's goalscoring form.

"She is always aggressive out of possession but also in possession. She scored a great header and controlled that really good ball from Alex Greenwood.

"That was really good athleticism and composure. Unfortunately that was disallowed but it was really good!

"Football is about scoring goals, but also playing in the pockets, keeping the ball and connecting with other players - and I was happy with her [doing those]."

Former England goalkeeper Rachel Brown-Finnis told BBC Radio 5 Live that Stanway was "unplayable at times" against Greece on Tuesday night.

She won all her tackles, had a 90% passing accuracy rate, took four shots, scored once and had another disallowed.

It was also a slightly different role for Stanway for most of the match as she played more as a right winger after changes in the midfield.

"She has something different to others," Wiegman told BBC Radio 5 Live.

"She is goal-orientated, has a great shot and the disallowed goal showed her great mobility and athleticism.

"When you really need a fight, or a duel, or a counter-attack breaking up, she is there. She is a warrior who you can play a possession game with too."

Tactical tweaks offer Wiegman fresh options

Stanway was even more effective in large part to a new-look midfield which included 20-year-old debutant Lexi Potter.

The Chelsea midfielder provided cover for the experienced Stanway and Keira Walsh to push higher up, while Lauren James played in the number 10 role.

It proved to be an inspired change from Wiegman as Stanway caused problems throughout for the visitors and was able to adapt to the tweaks impressively.

"Stanway has shown how flexible she is, how exceptional she is both at the bottom end of the pitch, breaking up play, as well as at the top end," added Brown-Finnis.

"She was playing as a second striker, playing out on the right, dropping deep as a number 10. She's been absolutely brilliant."

England still have a job to do to qualify for the 2027 Women's World Cup in Brazil with a two-legged play-off tie against Ukraine to navigate at the end of the year.

They have already beaten their opponents 9-1 on aggregate in two games of the league phase of the qualifiers.

After Wiegman's formation experiment worked so well this week, could it be an option for the future that brings out the best in Stanway, as well as others?

"I liked the balance of the midfield. There is a lot of competition going on in that area," admitted Wiegman.

"There were a few reasons. First of all, I wanted to see Lexi Potter deeper on the pitch and what that might bring.

"There was also the option to put Georgia Stanway higher up the pitch. We wanted to score more goals and we know that she can do that.

"She can play in the pocket and also deeper on the pitch so we wanted to see all of that."

articles.title: Northern Ireland: Michael McArdle 'really encouraged' despite Portugal loss
articles.summary: Northern Ireland manager Michael McArdle says their play-off defeat by Portugal is "the start of a new identity" despite their heavy 7-1 aggregate loss.
articles.body:
Northern Ireland manager Michael McArdle said their play-off defeat by Portugal is "the start of a new identity" despite their heavy 7-1 aggregate loss.

Portugal showed their ruthlessness during the first leg at Inver Park and had a four-goal advantage ahead of the second leg.

Kess Elmore's strike gave Northern Ireland the lead in Portimao, but the home side fought back and won 3-1 on the night.

"I'm really proud with the brave style of play but we have got to be patient moving forward," McArdle told BBC Sport NI.

"It's been a great camp for new players to come in. Now, I feel the profile of players, the energy they are bringing, the effort that they are putting in and the condition that they are in to compete at this level.

"I am really encouraged, personally, moving forward. I have said to the group that this is the start of a new move forward and the start of a new identity moving forward."

'Elmore is going to add so much to this group'

McArdle has shown throughout his tenure so far that he is keen to expand Northern Ireland's squad depth and gave four players their debuts during the Portugal double header.

One of those debutants, Elmore, scored Northern Ireland's only goal of the tie and became the second player to score on her debut under McArdle after Emily Cassap netted during the 2-1 defeat by Switzerland in June.

"I'm delighted for Kess," McArdle continued.

"I knew she could bring that, and it's just great that she has had that impact in Larne and also got the reward with a goal tonight.

"She's going to add so much to the group moving forward, but so will a lot of the debutants this week, which was exciting."

It has been a challenging window for McArdle's side with key players such as captain Simone Magill and the experienced Laura Rafferty, Nadene Caldwell and Caragh Hamilton missing.

However, the Scot still thinks the side have set "a real enthusiastic marker" down during the tough Portugal tie.

"There have been those moments that have went against us, moments of misfortune. We're playing a risky style of football," he continued.

"We were on the front foot from the first whistle, and I couldn't be prouder of the girls. This is a real enthusiastic marker for moving forward. This is getting closer to the identity that I would like for us moving forward.

"We want more energy, we want more mobility, and we want to be a lot more versatile as well. I'm really proud but also really frustrated with the scoreline."

Elmore nets on first start as Portugal beat NI

Northern Ireland's attentions will now turn to their preparation for the Nations League next year.

NI will compete in League B after finishing second in their group in 2025 before being beaten comfortably by Iceland in the promotion/relegation play-off.

"Against opposition like Portugal, I thought they were assured tonight in terms of their performance," said former Northern Ireland captain Marissa Callaghan.

"It does have that feel of something very special is going to come up. McArdle spoke about the next Nations League fixtures, he will be getting ready to start that campaign his way with his players and with his style.

articles.title: Bayern’s Michael Olise sent off for ‘super dumb’ yellows within seconds
articles.summary: Bayern Munich draw 3-3 with Viking in UEFA Champions League, but Michael Olise sees red for two bookings within seconds.
articles.body:
Bayern Munich were held 3-3 at Viking in the Champions League on Tuesday with the Norwegian champions equalising late through Herman Haugen after Michael Olise was sent off.

Bayern trailed 2-0 at halftime thanks to goals from Gianni Stensness and Peter Christiansen.

Harry Kane seemed to have dragged Bayern to victory as he scored twice and set up another for a 3-2 lead, but Olise saw a second yellow inside a minute for dissent after throwing the ball at an opponent’s face.

Viking made the most of their advantage with Haugen scoring in the final minute to snatch the Norwegian champions a shock draw against the German giants.

Olise’s red means he will miss next week’s blockbuster clash with English champions Arsenal in Munich.

“It was our own fault,” Kompany told reporters, adding “this red card was super dumb … You can see in (Michael’s) eyes that he’s sorry about it and that he regrets letting the team down.”

Kane scored for the ninth straight Champions League match, equalling a club record set by Robert Lewandowski and drawing two behind the record of 11 set by Cristiano Ronaldo.

“It was a poor first half from us. We started the second half well and fought our way back. But the red card changed everything,” Kane said on Amazon Prime.

“[Olise] will be gutted and he has to take responsibility for it. It was a mistake, and mistakes happen. He has to learn from it. It’s a shame because we have important games ahead of us.”

Just days after conceding the fastest goal in Bundesliga history in Saturday’s 2-2 draw at Augsburg, Bayern were again behind early.

With just 72 seconds gone, Stensness headed in an outswinging corner to give the hosts a shock lead.

Bayern ramped up the pressure but could not break through, with Kane twice heading into the waiting arms of Viking goalie Arild Ostbo.

Not content to absorb Bayern pressure and cling to a narrow lead, Viking launched a lightning-fast counter-attack and doubled their advantage after 38 minutes.

Top goalscorer Christiansen finished off a slick move to give Viking a 2-0 lead.

Bayern were handed a lifeline when Konrad Laimer was felled in the box just after the break, bringing Kane to the spot.

After a stuttering run up, the 33-year-old guided the ball into the bottom right of the goal, past the fingertips of Ostbo.

On the hour, Kane shed his marker and headed in a Joshua Kimmich cross to level the scores.

Diaz had an effort ruled out for offside just a minute later but the Colombian was the beneficiary of a brilliant Kane chip 10 minutes on.

Kane lofted a ball to Laimer, whose saved shot rebounded cleanly into Diaz’s path.

The England captain appeared to have saved Bayern, until Olise was sent from the pitch.

The France winger saw yellow for a foul and then picked up another when he threw the ball directly at Viking captain Zlatko Tripic’s face right in front of the referee, leaving Bayern a man down with 16 minutes left.

Viking pushed and Haugen headed in at the far post in the 90th minute to snatch the hosts a memorable draw.

articles.title: Arsenal 3-0 Lille: Bukayo Saka responds to challenge as fringe players have mixed night
articles.summary: Bukayo Saka responds to the challenge set by Mikel Arteta as he comes off the bench to change the game against Lille in the Champions League.
articles.body:
Bukayo Saka responded to the challenge set by Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta as he proved a game-changer in the 3-0 Champions League win over Lille.

The England forward has been told he should aim to score "two or three" goals per game - such was his quality and the expectation from his boss.

Saka did not achieve that tally against the French visitors, but shook off illness to come off the bench and assist Eberechi Eze's strike that made it 2-0, before rolling in his side's third goal.

The 25-year-old has now scored four goals in nine games this season and looks to be taking the next step in his evolution as Arsenal 's key man.

With the majority of his side's attacking play involving him, he has always been an influential figure. But with opposition defenders doubling up on him and injury issues over the last two seasons, there were doubts over whether Saka could still do what was asked of him in attack or if he had lost a yard of pace.

Arteta has tweaked Saka's positioning this season and, prior to Lille's visit, said it has been done deliberately to get him closer to the goal.

"That is where we need to get him," said the Gunners boss before the game. "And if he misses the chance, so be it. At the end, the more volume we generate, the bigger the probability of him scoring more goals."

Saka's strike against Lille was a confident one-touch finish and came after he missed a late one-on-one opportunity in Saturday's Premier League victory over Leeds .

"He has been getting in great positions, getting shots, getting one-touch finishes and tap-ins," added Arteta.

"That is the kind of unpredictability we have with that player, otherwise we know how the opponent is going to defend him. He is doing well, he could have had another four or five goals by now, easily. But if he continues like that, we know.

"When he talks about scoring a certain amount of goals, he needs to be thinking about scoring a certain amount of goals per game. If that shifts, that mentality, he will get into those positions and score more goals."

Saka has scored 20 goals in a season just once in his career, which came in the 2023-24 campaign and 16 in the Premier League.

But the winger has also been in good goalscoring form for England with five in his last four matches and scored a double in the 7-0 Nations League demolition of Croatia in the recent international break.

Saka is now on 19 goals in major European competitions for Arsenal , only behind Thierry Henry (42), while he has nine assists in the Champions League which puts him behind Henry (16) and Cesc Fabregas (14).

He has refused to disclose the targets he has set himself, but Arteta welcomed Saka's response following his message to do more in front of goal.

The Spaniard said: "I don't know if that's the case, but I am very happy.

"He wasn't feeling that good yesterday and today, as he had some sort of illness. He wasn't ready to start but he was really wanting to contribute to the team if it was needed and he came on and made a huge impact and delivered with real quality."

Arteta revealed he also spoke to Saka after telling the media about his desire for the player to have a greater impact.

"After the press conference... I said 'Bukayo, I just killed you in the press conference, good luck tomorrow'.

"He was laughing. He knows that we have discussed these kind of things and he takes it because he wants to be the best version of himself.

"In order to do that, you have to put big objectives and challenges and try to reason by working and being consistent - and when it doesn't work, keep going because he has the ability to do it."

Gyokeres struggles on mixed night for fringe players

Arteta made five changes to the team that started the win over Leeds as the Gunners looked to navigate six matches in all competitions during this month.

Noni Madueke moved to the right wing after putting in a good performance on the left at the weekend, with Mikel Merino, Eze and Viktor Gyokeres all coming into the starting XI.

Eze had started just two games in all competitions before the match with Lille and Arteta had said his attitude had been "phenomenal" despite a lack of game time.

The 28-year-old showed flashes of his undoubted quality and his finish for Arsenal 's second goal - and his first of the season - will give him confidence going forward.

Madueke had a mixed night as he showed his ability to beat a defender, but questions remain over his end product - even if he provided the assist for Jurrien Timber's classy opening goal.

However, it was not a good night for Gyokeres.

The Sweden striker scored 21 goals in all competitions last season as Arsenal won the title for the first time in 22 years and displayed his willingness to run and work hard.

But Gyokeres had just 12 touches before being replaced and Kai Havertz, as he so often does, looked a much better and more natural fit for the Arsenal frontline, teeing up Saka's goal too.

Arteta brought on Saka, Havertz and Martin Odegaard after going 1-0 up and all three contributed to show why they are still the first names on the teamsheet and why the Arsenal boss will be so reliant on them if they are to achieve more honours.

articles.title: Packers Sign Rookie Cornerback After Bears Win
articles.summary: The Green Bay Packers tried out three players on Monday after their Week 5 win over the Chicago Bears. They looked at two defensive backs and one defensive t...
articles.body:
The Green Bay Packers tried out three players on Monday after their Week 5 win over the Chicago Bears. They looked at two defensive backs and one defensive tackle. Their first move is to sign one of the defensive backs to the practice squad.

According to the league transaction wire, the Packers signed cornerback Elijah Culp to their practice squad and released guard Josh Gesky.

Green Bay Packers Sign CB Elijah Culp to Practice Squad

Culp is a rookie UDFA, but he has bounced around a lot, from college to the NFL. He started his college career at Austin Peay. However, he moved up to Troy the following year. He stayed at Troy for two years, but suffered an injury in 2022 and missed the entire 2023 season.

In 2024, he transferred to Charlotte. Then, in 2025, he moved on to James Madison. He started in 13 games, but still went undrafted.

In the NFL, he signed with the Arizona Cardinals directly after the NFL Draft. He did not stick with them after roster cuts and eventually found his way to the Indianapolis Colts . However, they released him from their practice squad.

Gesky was a 2026 UDFA as well. He spent the majority of training camp and the preseason at right guard. However, the Packers signed Kevin Zeitler at right guard, and Travis Glover moved from tackle inside to right guard. So, the team is now much deeper at guard than it was prior to this.

The Packers practice squad currently has Kedon Slovis at quarterback. They have Damon Bankston as their running back now that Pierre Strong is signed to the active roster. At receiver, the Packers have three practice squad options.

Isaiah Neyor, Quincy Skinner, and Coleman Owen make up the three options that could get called up now that Skyy Moore is banged up.

At tight end, the team has Drake Dabney. Mekhi Becton is another right guard option on the practice squad, making Gesky more expendable. Dillon Wade is another offensive line option. They also have Dalton Cooper, although he is a tackle.

On the edge, the Packers have rookie UDFA Nyjalik Kelly and Arron Mosby. They also have defensive tackle David Blay. Then, at linebacker, it is the recently signed Jack Dingle.

Their cornerback is rookie sixth-round pick Domani Jackson. He cleared waivers and circled back. Now, they will have Culp in addition to him. Kahlef Hailassaie is their practice squad safety, and the team even has a kicker on their practice squad. Lenny Krieg is the current kicker on the practice squad.

Green Bay will take on the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday Night Football in Week 6.

articles.title: Dan Orlovsky believes Broncos QB Bo Nix’s off form is worse than Drake Maye’s woes
articles.summary: At 3-2, the Denver Broncos are tied with the Las Vegas Raiders for second in the AFC West. Both teams are a game and a half behind the Kansas City Chiefs, wh...
articles.body:
At 3-2, the Denver Broncos are tied with the Las Vegas Raiders for second in the AFC West. Both teams are a game and a half behind the Kansas City Chiefs, who are undefeated at 4-0. While the Chiefs come off an early bye, the Broncos and Raiders both face difficult matchups against the Seahawks and Bills, respectively. Ahead of their Thursday Night Football tilt against Seattle, NFL analyst Dan Orlovsky broke down why Denver quarterback Bo Nix has struggled so far this season. Orlovsky shared his analysis via X, formerly Twitter.

"I think the significant regression right now with Bo Nix is very process-driven in regards to completely derailing timing and rhythm," Orlovsky broke down on Tuesday evening.

Nix is completing just under 60 percent of his passes, a career low. The former first-round pick has thrown for only 942 yards and six touchdowns, to go with three interceptions. He's thrown for over 250 yards only once this season, in the Broncos' Week 2 win over the Jacksonville Jaguars. He's coming off his lowest passing yardage mark of the season, only gaining 123 yards through the air in a 23-17 win over the Los Angeles Chargers, a division rival.

If the Broncos hope to get back to the top of the AFC West, they need Nix to improve upon his form from last year. In his sophomore campaign, Nix led Denver to the AFC's top seed, plus an AFC Championship Game berth. A broken ankle at the end of their AFC Divisional matchup win over the Buffalo Bills ended Nix's season. Now, it feels like he's out of sync. If he can't get back on track, then the Broncos might not reach the heights of last fall.
